hero.label: Overview
hero.title: An enterprise-grade design system I built alone, with real Figma-to-code parity

accent.note: Verified Figma-to-code parity — built solo, over one calendar month of intermittent work.

context.label: Context & stakes
context.title: Can an AI-built system hold real governance, or is it surface-level craft?
paragraphs: After years leading design systems with teams of dozens at Elastic and VMware, I wanted a direct test: can an AI-built design system hold the same level of governance and brand fidelity as one built by a full team — or does the result end up as surface-level craft with no corporate foundations underneath?

My hypothesis: domain knowledge, not headcount, is what holds a real system together. If that’s true, the same rigor should survive even when the person directing understands the domain but the one executing is a model.
A second, harder test ran alongside it: that the library would hold up when used to compose layouts I didn’t hand-design myself — not just display each component in isolation.

rows.label: MY ROLE
rows.body: AI Design Systems Leader — owned direction, governance and decision-making at every layer (taxonomy, tokens, accessibility, architecture). I delegated execution to Claude, under skills I designed and governed myself.

rows.label: DURATION
rows.body: 1 month (calendar) — intermittent work, never full-time. Original goal was under 3 months; I landed earlier and with fewer hours than budgeted.

rows.label: TEAM
rows.body: Solo, end-to-end. No human collaborators — I delegated execution to Claude under my direction and approval at every stage.

rows.label: SCOPE
rows.body: Personal brand system (Viu): foundations, 73 Figma components (29 atoms · 35 molecules · 9 organisms + 4 patterns), the @viu/ui library in React with Storybook, and the NataliaRS/Viu repo.

rows.label: TOOLS
rows.body: Figma (+ MCP) · Claude · Claude Code · Storybook · React

frame.label: Strategic frame
frame.title: "Use AI to design faster" was the tempting framing. I chose a harder one.
paragraphs: The easy version of this project was "use AI to go faster." The version I actually ran: keep the same real tools — Figma for design, real code for production — and use AI as the executor under my direction, not as an autonomous generator.
My hypothesis: design-to-code parity and absolute brand fidelity don’t have to be sacrificed when the person directing understands the domain, even if the one executing is a model.

Every process was new — taxonomy, skills, Figma-to-code verification flows — I defined them as I went, with no prior template, no added headcount, and no new budget line: just my existing Claude and ChatGPT accounts.

moves.title: 01 · Master skill
moves.body: Before touching a component, I fixed brand identity and locks, governance, a universal pre-flight check that forces verification of Figma’s real state before every change, and skill updates at the close of every batch — so knowledge wouldn’t get lost between sessions.

moves.title: 02 · Reference skills
moves.body: On top of that scaffolding: component taxonomy, token and state canon, and technical Figma learnings — like loadAsync() being mandatory before reading children, or that an instance’s internals don’t surface with findAll().

moves.title: 03 · Taxonomy
moves.body: Foundations → Components → Patterns, with explicit rules so similar-looking categories don’t collapse into each other: Badge and Tag communicate state, not interactive; Pill and Chip are actioned; Notification badge overlays something else.

moves.title: 04 · Execution with parity, functional on both sides
moves.body: Claude connected to Figma via MCP, with the full library built in code (NataliaRS/Viu) and parity verified at every step — a continuous loop where Figma is the single source of truth, not a one-time migration.

moves.title: 05 · Storybook as a product, not documentation
moves.body: The full Viu brand applied to Storybook itself: a built-in accessibility check per component, a two-language toggle, a light/dark toggle per panel, and a direct link from every component to its Figma node.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.title: What holds it up.
evidence.lead: Not a claim — a set of specific, checkable decisions.
items: My contrast audit corrected success-solid.light from green.600 to green.700 to meet WCAG AA (7.48:1) — not an aesthetic call, an accessibility decision backed by a number.
I had mis-canonized the "disabled" mechanism using opacity; reverted it to explicit tokens (bg-disabled/text-disabled) as soon as I caught it.
Border-contrast failures are documented as accepted exceptions under WCAG 1.4.11 — not ignored gaps.
The 73/74/77 reconciliation (Figma / publishable folders / manifest) was investigated component by component until every difference had a named cause, instead of accepting it as "expected noise."
The accessibility check lives inside Storybook, at the individual component level — not as an external audit separate from the daily workflow.
Every component links directly to its Figma node — parity isn’t a claim, it’s verifiable with one click from the same place where the component is consumed.

I ran test-and-learn experiments in the Figma sandbox: recomposing reference layouts from other brands using only existing Viu components, with no ad hoc pieces — validating that the taxonomy and tokens hold real compositions, not just isolated demos.

outcomes.label: Outcomes
outcomes.title: What it measures — and what it doesn’t.

items.label: FIGMA COMPONENTS
items.body: 29 atoms · 35 molecules · 9 organisms + 4 patterns — built from zero, with no prior system, over one month of intermittent work.

items.label: VERIFIED FIGMA-TO-CODE PARITY
items.body: 74 publishable folders in @viu/ui against 77 manifest entries — the difference of 3 is traced and explained, not an unaudited gap.

items.label: TEAM OF ONE
items.body: No added headcount, no new budget, no collaborators — every direction and execution decision under my own responsibility.

items.label: QUALITY GATES PASSING GREEN
items.body: Contrast audit (WCAG), token-usage audit, orphan-component ghost-check, and literal linting — automated verification, not a "vibe-coded" system.

outcomes.note: These are craft and build-velocity metrics, not adoption or business-impact metrics — Viu doesn’t have real users yet.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.title: What I’d do differently.
reflection.body: I’d build the universal pre-flight check into the master skill from the first commit — I lost time twice from not calling loadAsync() before reading Figma’s real state. I’d also decide upfront how many languages I need, instead of adding that later. The real work wasn’t done by the AI: it was years of knowing how design systems actually work that made it possible to hold this together as one person. A big part of the process was teaching the AI the unwritten rules a senior designer applies without thinking — without that explicit teaching, the result doesn’t reach the level I need.
